# Epic 8 Context: Evolution Dashboard & Account Management

<!-- Compiled from planning artifacts. Edit freely. Regenerate with compile-epic-context if planning docs change. -->

## Goal

Users can see an on-demand chart of their journaling activity with an independent AI narrative, edit their display name, log out, and permanently delete their account and all associated data. This is the final build unit in the delivery order — it assumes every earlier unit (entries, auth, chat, export) already exists, since the dashboard has nothing to aggregate without entries and account actions rely on the auth session already established in F000.

## Stories

- Story 8.1: On-Demand Dashboard Aggregation Across Entry Counts
- Story 8.2: Independent Narrative Text & Narrative-Unavailable State
- Story 8.3: Profile Name Editing
- Story 8.4: Logout
- Story 8.5: Account Deletion

## Requirements & Constraints

- The evolution chart is computed fresh every time the settings screen opens — never served from a stale local cache — and must render correctly at exactly three entry-count scenarios: zero, one, and more than thirty. These counts are fixed and not re-tunable.
- The narrative paragraph is a separate network call from the chart data, by design: the two must never be coupled so that a narrative failure cannot block or hide a chart that has valid data.
- Aggregation must recalculate whenever a new entry is created anywhere in the app; because entries are immutable (never edited), invalidation only ever needs to trigger on create.
- Account deletion is a hard, permanent delete of the account and all associated data (LGPD-driven) — not a soft delete or deactivation.
- No dedicated "account deleted" confirmation screen exists for this delivery; both logout and account deletion dead-end at the same login/vault destination.
- The persona selector shown on this screen is a cosmetic, non-functional placeholder only (an extension feature) — it must never appear to change assistant behavior.
- Every acceptance criterion for this epic's FRs must pass as the primary success measure; no automated performance instrumentation is required beyond a manual spot-check against the product's general UI-latency thresholds.
- Standard cross-cutting rules apply: no Clean Architecture layer violations, repository methods return `Either<Failure, T>` with no unmapped exceptions, and no visual value is hardcoded outside the design-tokens source.

## Technical Decisions

- Two features own this epic's work: a `dashboard` feature (chart + narrative aggregation/rendering) and a separate `account` feature (persona-toggle placeholder, profile edit, logout, delete account). Both are thin — standard layer-dependency and Either-error-channel rules apply, nothing feature-specific beyond that.
- The dashboard screen uses the shared `Resource<T>` (`idle`/`loading`/`data`/`error`) view-state type, since it is a single-source, single-fetch-lifecycle screen — do not build a one-off state shape for it, and do not force the narrative fetch into the same `Resource<T>` instance as the chart (they are independent fetches, each can be its own `Resource<T>` if a second one is needed).
- The dashboard is explicitly excluded from the local offline-cache pattern used by entries/chat — it has no `hive_ce` box and is never served from cache; each screen visit is a live fetch. Cache-invalidation behavior for the chart (recalculating after a new entry) is a presentation-layer concern owned by whoever builds this epic, not a shared local-cache mechanism.
- This epic extends the minimal settings-screen stub already scaffolded earlier in the project rather than recreating the screen.
- The 52px avatar shown here reuses the same avatar component already built earlier (previously only used at a 40px size) — do not reimplement it.
- Charting uses `fl_chart` (already pinned for the project).

## UX & Interaction Patterns

- Dashboard empty/sparse states: zero entries shows a placeholder chart icon and "Comece a registrar..." with no summary text at all (nothing to summarize, not a failure); exactly one entry shows a single bar with "Ainda é cedo pra ver um padrão..."; more than thirty entries shows a 10-bar chart with the AI narrative paragraph below it.
- Narrative-unavailable is a distinct visual state from the zero-entries empty state: when only the narrative call fails, the chart still renders normally and a clear "narrative unavailable" message appears in its place — never a blank space, never conflated with having no data.
- Profile name editing: tapping the pencil icon beside the name switches it to an inline editable field and the pencil icon itself changes to a check icon — the only place in the product where an icon's meaning changes rather than just its color. Confirming saves and reverts to display mode; tapping away without confirming also reverts to display mode. There is no separate "edit profile" screen.
- The account-deletion confirmation dialog uses a red (`colorError`) title — the only product-wide pattern where title color (not just an icon or badge) is the signal distinguishing an irreversible action from a routine interruption like session expiry (which uses a neutral title). This color must never be muted or reused for non-destructive confirmations.
- The account-deletion dialog traps focus until dismissed or confirmed, reusing the same focus-trap overlay behavior already used by the session-expired overlay — no interacting with the scrim-covered screen underneath while it's open.
- General overlay conventions apply: a scrim fades in first, the dialog/sheet sits at most one level deep over the base screen, and under reduced-motion settings the scrim/entrance animation is skipped in favor of showing the final state immediately.

## Cross-Story Dependencies

- Story 8.2's narrative text is fetched independently alongside Story 8.1's chart, but visually appears only once the chart from 8.1 is already rendering — 8.1 must ship the chart and its three entry-count states before 8.2's narrative/unavailable states are meaningful to build on top of.
- Story 8.3 depends on the avatar component already built in an earlier epic; it must be reused at a new fixed size, not reimplemented.
- Story 8.5's focus-trap dialog behavior depends on the same focus-trap pattern already implemented for the session-expired overlay elsewhere in the app; reuse it rather than building a second implementation.
- Stories 8.4 and 8.5 both route to the same post-action destination (the login/vault screen) — keep that destination logic shared rather than duplicated between logout and account deletion.
- The whole epic depends on entries existing (for the dashboard to have anything to aggregate) and on the auth session mechanism built in the foundation unit (for logout/deletion to have a session to end).

---
title: 'Story 8.4: Logout'
type: 'feature'
created: '2026-11-08'
status: 'done'
review_loop_iteration: 0
context: []
baseline_commit: '150b89db7aef65fe75834a13d23f4af76cffe260'
---

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** Configurações has no way to end the session — "Sair" is a dead action (epic-8-context.md's Story 8.4 scope; FR-42, RF03).

**Approach:** Add `logout()`/`lock()`/`clearLocalCache()` to `SessionRepository`/`VaultRepository`/`EntriesRepository`/`ChatRepository` respectively; `AccountSettingsCubit` orchestrates all four behind one `logout()` call triggered by a new "Sair" button. No new navigation code — the existing `app_router.dart` redirect (already watching both streams) takes the user to Biometria once the vault relocks.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- `SessionRepository.logout()` (mirrors `restoreSession()`): calls new `AuthRemoteDataSource.logout()` (`POST auth-logout`, bearerAuth, no body), then UNCONDITIONALLY calls `AccessTokenProvider.clearSession()` and emits `SessionStatus.unauthenticated` — must work even offline.
- `VaultRepository.lock()` (new, sync, mirrors `markAuthenticated()`): `_emit(VaultStatus.locked)`. Cubit calls this BEFORE awaiting `sessionRepository.logout()` — AD-14's vault-gate-first redirect then lands on `/vault` (Biometria) with no transient `/auth` hop (prototype-extract.md:40-41, Story 8.5 shares this destination).
- `EntriesRepository`/`ChatRepository` gain `clearLocalCache()` (`Either<Failure, Unit>`, `try`/`catch` around box `.clear()`) — closes deferred-work.md's "no clear-on-logout hook" gap now that a logout feature exists.
- `AccountSettingsCubit` gains the 4 repos above as constructor deps (same direct-domain-interface precedent as `EntryDetailCubit`→`SessionRepository`) + `logout()`: guard re-entry via new `isLoggingOut`, `vaultRepository.lock()`, `await sessionRepository.logout()` (result ignored — local session already ended regardless), `await Future.wait([entries.clearLocalCache(), chat.clearLocalCache()])`, same `isClosed` guard as `toggleBiometric`.
- Screen: `AppButton(secondaryOutline, 'Sair', onPressed: state.isLoggingOut ? null : cubit.logout)` as the scroll column's last child, below `DashboardChartSection`.

**Ask First:** None.

**Never:** `sl.reset()`/re-running `setupCoreDependencies()` (strands `_CerneAppState`'s captured repo instances); clearing in-memory cubit/tracker state — scoped to only the two Hive boxes deferred-work.md names; an "Apagar conta" button/dialog (Story 8.5); surfacing a backend-logout-failure error.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Tap Sair | `isLoggingOut: false` | vault relocks immediately -> router redirects to `/vault`; `auth-logout` fires; local tokens + both Hive boxes clear | N/A |
| `auth-logout` backend call fails (offline/expired/...) | any | local session still clears, same redirect | `Left` swallowed, no UI message |
| Double-tap Sair | `isLoggingOut: true` | second tap no-ops (button disabled) | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/features/auth/domain/repositories/session_repository.dart` / `data/repositories/session_repository_impl.dart:117-173` -- add + implement `logout()`, mirrors `restoreSession()`
- `lib/features/auth/data/datasources/auth_remote_data_source.dart:21-24` -- add `logout()` (`_apiClient.post('auth-logout')` -> `Either<Failure, Unit>`); `test/features/auth/data/datasources/auth_remote_data_source_test.dart` -- direct coverage of this call
- `lib/features/vault/domain/repositories/vault_repository.dart` / `data/repositories/vault_repository_impl.dart:139-158` (`_emit`) -- add + implement `lock()`
- `lib/features/entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart` / `data/repositories/entries_repository_impl.dart:21-29` (`_entriesBox`) -- add `clearLocalCache()`
- `lib/features/chat/domain/repositories/chat_repository.dart` / `data/repositories/chat_repository_impl.dart:21-32` (`_sessionsBox`/`_messagesBox`) -- add `clearLocalCache()`
- `lib/features/account/presentation/cubit/account_settings_cubit.dart:148-171` -- constructor deps + `isLoggingOut` + `logout()`
- `lib/features/account/presentation/screens/account_settings_screen.dart:429-540` -- "Sair" `AppButton`, after `DashboardChartSection`
- `lib/features/account/account_injection.dart:34-37` -- widen `AccountSettingsCubit` registration with the 4 new `sl<...>()` deps
- `lib/core/widgets/app_button.dart` -- reused as-is (`secondaryOutline`)
- `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml:292-313` (`auth-logout`, bearerAuth) + `README.md:28`
- `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md:40-41,116` -- "Sair" → Biometria; only "Apagar conta" (Story 8.5) is red
- `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/deferred-work.md` (spec-3-1's "no clear-on-logout hook" entry) -- the gap this story closes
- `test/features/{auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl,vault/data/repositories/vault_repository_impl,entries/data/repositories/entries_repository_impl,chat/data/repositories/chat_repository_impl,account/presentation/cubit/account_settings_cubit,account/presentation/screens/account_settings_screen}_test.dart` -- extend fakes/mocks + new coverage

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [x] `session_repository.dart`/`_impl.dart` -- `logout()`
- [x] `auth_remote_data_source.dart` -- `logout()`
- [x] `vault_repository.dart`/`_impl.dart` -- `lock()`
- [x] `entries_repository.dart`/`_impl.dart` -- `clearLocalCache()`
- [x] `chat_repository.dart`/`_impl.dart` -- `clearLocalCache()`
- [x] `account_settings_cubit.dart` -- constructor deps, `isLoggingOut`, `logout()`
- [x] `account_settings_screen.dart` -- "Sair" button
- [x] `account_injection.dart` -- widen registration
- [x] Tests: I/O matrix + new unit coverage for every new repository method; update `AccountSettingsCubit`'s fakes for the widened constructor

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given Configurações, when "Sair" is tapped, then `POST /auth/logout` fires and the user is routed to the Biometric Vault screen (epics.md Story 8.4 AC).
- Given the backend call fails, then the user is still routed away with no error shown (local session already ended).
- Given logout completes, then the entries and chat Hive boxes are empty (deferred-work.md gap closed).

### Review Findings

- [x] [Review][Patch] The narrative-unavailable `listenWhen` guard (spec-8-3's own patch, added in this same diff) doesn't actually stop repeat announcements: `DashboardCubit.load()` always emits `ResourceLoading` before `ResourceData`, so the state immediately before any `confirmedWrites`-triggered reload's qualifying `ResourceData` is `ResourceLoading`, not a qualifying `ResourceData` — the `!(previous is ResourceData<DashboardAggregate> && previous.data.totalCount > 30)` clause is therefore true again every time, so the listener still re-announces "narrativa indisponível" on every subsequent reload while `totalCount > 30`, the exact bug this fix was written to close. [account_settings_screen.dart:518-522] — fixed: replaced the `listenWhen` transition-comparison with a `_dashboardOverflowAnnounced` field tracked across actual `ResourceData` emissions only (ignoring the interleaved `ResourceLoading`s), reset only on an explicit crossing back to `totalCount <= 30`.
- [x] [Review][Patch] `tests/test-summary.md`'s Verification section (added by this diff) reports `1251/1251 passed` / `this round added: 9`, scoped only to story 8.3's two new e2e groups — no corresponding entry covers story 8.4's own substantial test additions in this same commit (`account_settings_cubit_test.dart`, `account_settings_screen_test.dart`, `auth_remote_data_source_test.dart`, `session_repository_impl_test.dart`, `chat_repository_impl_test.dart`, `entries_repository_impl_test.dart`, `vault_repository_impl_test.dart`), so the reported pass count/delta is stale for this diff's actual scope. [_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/tests/test-summary.md] — fixed: re-ran `fvm flutter test`/`fvm flutter analyze` (1276/1276 passed, 0 analyze issues) and appended a addendum section with the real total and +25 delta.
- [x] [Review][Patch] `AccountSettingsState.displayName`'s field doc comment still says it is "kept in sync by `confirmEditingName`'s own success branch — never re-read from the repository afterwards," but this diff's own change to that exact success branch now does `displayName: _repository.currentDisplayName` specifically to re-read it — the comment contradicts the behavior the diff introduces a few lines below it. [account_settings_cubit.dart:46-50] — fixed: comment now describes the re-read.
- [x] [Review][Patch] This spec's own "Suggested Review Order" anchors "the re-entry guard... the Sair button's disabled state depends on" at `account_settings_cubit.dart:85` — that line is the `isLoggingOut` field *declaration*, not the guard check (`if (state.isLoggingOut) return;`, actually at line 349). [spec-8-4-logout.md, Suggested Review Order] — fixed: anchor corrected to the guard's actual (now-current) line.
- [x] [Review][Patch] This spec's own Code Map test-file list omits `auth_remote_data_source_test.dart`, even though this same document's Spec Change Log item 3 and Suggested Review Order both state that file gained new direct coverage of `logout()`. [spec-8-4-logout.md, Code Map] — fixed: added to the Code Map bullet.
- [x] [Review][Patch] Cache-clear failure diagnostics lose which box failed: `ChatRepositoryImpl.clearLocalCache()` collapses `_sessionsBox`/`_messagesBox` errors into one untagged `firstError`, and `AccountSettingsCubit.logout()`'s `debugPrint` on a `Left` result doesn't say whether it came from `entries` or `chat` — a real disk-full failure would be unattributable from logs alone. [chat_repository_impl.dart:163; account_settings_cubit.dart:358] — fixed: both now tag the box/repository name into the failure message.
- [x] [Review][Patch] `AccountSettingsCubit.logout()` has no `try/finally` around its `await` chain — if `_vaultRepository.lock()`/`_sessionRepository.logout()`/`clearLocalCache()` ever throws instead of returning `Left` (none currently do, but nothing enforces that), `isLoggingOut` would stay `true` forever, permanently disabling the "Sair" button. [account_settings_cubit.dart:348-358] — fixed: wrapped the chain in `try`/`finally`, resetting `isLoggingOut` unconditionally.
- [x] [Review][Defer] `SessionRepositoryImpl.logout()` swallows a `clearSession()` exception with an empty `catch (_) {}` and no logging, while the cache-clear failures a few lines away in the same logout flow (`AccountSettingsCubit.logout()`) do `debugPrint`. [session_repository_impl.dart:183] — on inspection, this silent catch deliberately mirrors `restoreSession()`'s own pre-existing identical silent-catch convention in this same file (same comment cites it); adding `debugPrint` here would deviate from that established, intentional match rather than fix a defect. Reclassified from Patch to Defer — a codebase-wide tension between two valid local conventions (this file's silent-catch vs. the cubit layer's debugPrint-on-failure), not a bug this diff introduced. — deferred, pre-existing
- [x] [Review][Defer] The "Sair" button shows no loading indicator while `isLoggingOut` is true (just `onPressed: null`) — every other in-flight async action on this screen (name save, biometric toggle) shows a `CircularProgressIndicator`. [account_settings_screen.dart:577] — reclassified from Patch to Defer: `AppButton` is a shared primitive with no loading-slot API, reused across login/signup/entries/vault; adding one here means either changing that shared widget (out of this story's scope) or a layout change around it that can't be visually verified (no simulator/device in this project yet). Low-impact in practice since the vault-lock-triggered redirect fires near-instantly. — deferred, pre-existing
- [x] [Review][Defer] `EntriesRepository.clearLocalCache()`/`ChatRepository.clearLocalCache()` use `Failure.malformedResponse` for local Hive disk-clear failures — a type named for malformed network responses, not local-storage faults. Mirrors an existing convention already used elsewhere in the codebase; fixing it means a broader `Failure`-taxonomy change outside this story's scope. [entries_repository_impl.dart:234; chat_repository_impl.dart:163] — deferred, pre-existing
- [x] [Review][Defer] The vault locks and the router can redirect to `/vault` before the awaited `auth-logout` call and the two `clearLocalCache()` calls finish; if the OS kills the app in that window, the backend session may stay un-revoked and/or the Hive caches unflushed. Generic mobile async-during-navigation risk, not unique to this story's design, and out of scope to mitigate here (would need background-task handling). [account_settings_cubit.dart:348-358] — deferred, pre-existing
- [x] [Review][Defer] `AccountSettingsCubit.logout()` doesn't guard against `toggleBiometric`/`confirmEditingName` being in flight when "Sair" is tapped — a resolved in-flight call can `emit()` after logout, stomping state with results computed before the session ended. Same root cause and risk class as this story's own already-recorded "logout never resets in-memory singleton state" deferral; not fixable without the broader in-memory-reset decision already explicitly scoped out of this story's frozen Boundaries. [account_settings_cubit.dart:209-235] — deferred, pre-existing
- [x] [Review][Defer] No real-DI (`sl<...>()`-resolved) e2e test exists yet for the logout orchestration end-to-end, unlike biometric-toggle/name-edit's own `account_settings_flow_e2e_test.dart` coverage — a fakes-based router test (`pumpWithLogoutFakesAndVaultGate`) already proves the lock-before-redirect ordering, so this is a coverage-depth gap, not a correctness gap. The test-file changes are a separate, not-yet-reviewed chunk of this diff; revisit there or as a follow-up. [test/features/account/account_settings_flow_e2e_test.dart] — deferred, pre-existing

## Spec Change Log

- Post-implementation review (3-layer: blind-hunter, edge-case-hunter, verification-gap) found 4 trivially-fixable issues, all applied:
  1. `ChatRepositoryImpl.clearLocalCache()` now clears `_sessionsBox`/`_messagesBox` independently (separate try/catch each) so a throw on one never skips the other.

Cross-story (epic-8-context.md): Story 8.5 (account deletion) reuses this same lock+logout+clear sequence after its own `DELETE /account` call — write `AccountSettingsCubit.logout()` so that story can call it (or extract a shared private helper) rather than duplicating it.

1	import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
2	
3	import '../design_tokens.dart';
4	import 'app_button.dart';
5	
6	/// Shared confirmation-dialog overlay (prototype-extract.md §6: "scrim +
7	/// centered card; neutral title (session) or red title (destructive
8	/// deletion)"). Story 1.5 is the first consumer (neutral `colorTextPrimary`
9	/// title, the session-expiry recovery copy); a later story (Epic 8's
10	/// account-deletion confirm) reuses this same widget with [titleColor]
11	/// set to `DesignTokens.colorError` and a heavier [barrierColor].
12	///
13	/// UX-DR16/25/27/36: non-dismissible barrier, focus trapped on the dialog,
14	/// `scrimIn` (0.18s ease-out fade) as the only entrance choreography, and
15	/// at most one instance open at a time — [show] is the one way this
16	/// widget is ever presented, and owns that single-overlay guard itself so
17	/// no caller has to re-implement it.
18	class ConfirmationDialog extends StatelessWidget {
19	  const ConfirmationDialog({
20	    super.key,
21	    required this.icon,
22	    required this.title,
23	    required this.message,
24	    required this.confirmLabel,
25	    required this.onConfirm,
26	    required this.barrierColor,
27	    this.titleColor = DesignTokens.colorTextPrimary,
28	    this.caption,
29	  });
30	
31	  final IconData icon;
32	  final String title;
33	  final String message;
34	  final String confirmLabel;
35	  final VoidCallback onConfirm;
36	
37	  /// The full-bleed scrim color behind the centered card — callers pass
38	  /// `DesignTokens.colorScrim` (session-expiry, Story 1.5) or the heavier
39	  /// drawer/sheet value a later story uses for its own confirmation.
40	  final Color barrierColor;
41	
42	  /// Neutral (`colorTextPrimary`, the default — Story 1.5's session copy)
43	  /// or destructive (`colorError`, a later story's account-deletion
44	  /// confirm) — never any other color (Boundaries: "neutral
45	  /// `colorTextPrimary` title, never `colorError`" for *this* story's own
46	  /// call site).
47	  final Color titleColor;
48	
49	  /// Small mono caption below the button (Story 1.5: "o histórico e a
50	  /// posição do scroll são preservados"). Optional — a future destructive
51	  /// confirmation has no equivalent.
52	  final String? caption;
53	
54	  /// Whether an instance is currently showing — the single-overlay guard
55	  /// (UX-DR16/25/27/36: "never stacks on another open overlay"). Exposed
56	  /// for tests; callers should not need to read it directly.
57	  static bool isOpen = false;
58	
59	  /// Presents [builder]'s [ConfirmationDialog] as a non-dismissible,
60	  /// focus-trapped overlay above whatever screen is currently showing,
61	  /// without replacing it — the underlying route stays mounted, so its
62	  /// scroll/state is preserved (Boundaries: "the authenticated screen's
63	  /// widget instance is never replaced").
64	  ///
65	  /// A second call while one is already open is a silent no-op (I/O
66	  /// matrix: "already-open overlay ... no second dialog stacks").
67	  static Future<void> show({
68	    required BuildContext context,
69	    required WidgetBuilder builder,
70	  }) {
71	    if (isOpen) {
72	      return Future<void>.value();
73	    }
74	    isOpen = true;
75	    try {
76	      return showGeneralDialog<void>(
77	        context: context,
78	        barrierDismissible: false,
79	        // The framework's own `ModalBarrier` stays fully transparent — the
80	        // scrim actually seen on screen is this widget's own `build()`
81	        // below, which lets `transitionBuilder` fade the scrim and the card
82	        // together as one `scrimIn` choreography instead of two separately
83	        // animated layers.
84	        barrierColor: Colors.transparent,
85	        transitionDuration: const Duration(milliseconds: 180),
86	        transitionBuilder: (context, animation, secondaryAnimation, child) {
87	          return FadeTransition(
88	            opacity: CurvedAnimation(parent: animation, curve: Curves.easeOut),
89	            child: child,
90	          );
91	        },
92	        pageBuilder: (context, animation, secondaryAnimation) => PopScope(
93	          // UX-DR16/25/27/36 — non-dismissible: `barrierDismissible: false`
94	          // above only stops a scrim tap; without this, the system/hardware
95	          // back gesture would still pop the route and close the overlay.
96	          canPop: false,
97	          child: builder(context),
98	        ),
99	      ).whenComplete(() => isOpen = false);
100	    } catch (_) {
101	      // A synchronous throw from `showGeneralDialog` (e.g. a future caller
102	      // passing a `context` with no `Navigator` ancestor) must still release
103	      // the guard — otherwise every later `show()` call, from any caller,
104	      // silently no-ops forever.
105	      isOpen = false;
106	      rethrow;
107	    }
108	  }
109	
110	  @override
111	  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
112	    return Stack(
113	      fit: StackFit.expand,
114	      children: [
115	        ColoredBox(color: barrierColor),
116	        // `LayoutBuilder` + `ConstrainedBox(minHeight: ...)` is the
117	        // standard "centered, but scrollable if it doesn't fit" shape:
118	        // ordinary-scale content still centers vertically exactly as
119	        // before (the min-height constraint is satisfied with room to
120	        // spare, so `Center` centers within it), but under an extreme
121	        // Dynamic Type scale — where the card's intrinsic height can
122	        // exceed the screen — this scrolls instead of overflowing
123	        // (RNF08's "no control truncates under Dynamic Type").
124	        LayoutBuilder(
125	          builder: (context, constraints) => SingleChildScrollView(
126	            child: ConstrainedBox(
127	              constraints: BoxConstraints(minHeight: constraints.maxHeight),
128	              child: Center(
129	                child: Padding(
130	                  padding: DesignTokens.dialogScreenMargin,
131	                  child: _Card(
132	                    icon: icon,
133	                    title: title,
134	                    titleColor: titleColor,
135	                    message: message,
136	                    confirmLabel: confirmLabel,
137	                    onConfirm: onConfirm,
138	                    caption: caption,
139	                  ),
140	                ),
141	              ),
142	            ),
143	          ),
144	        ),
145	      ],
146	    );
147	  }
148	}
149	
150	class _Card extends StatelessWidget {
151	  const _Card({
152	    required this.icon,
153	    required this.title,
154	    required this.titleColor,
155	    required this.message,
156	    required this.confirmLabel,
157	    required this.onConfirm,
158	    required this.caption,
159	  });

162	  final String title;
163	  final Color titleColor;
164	  final String message;
165	  final String confirmLabel;
166	  final VoidCallback onConfirm;
167	  final String? caption;
168	
169	  @override
170	  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
171	    return Container(
172	      padding: DesignTokens.dialogCardPadding,
173	      decoration: const BoxDecoration(
174	        color: DesignTokens.colorSurfaceElevated,
175	        borderRadius: BorderRadius.all(Radius.circular(DesignTokens.radiusLg)),
176	        boxShadow: DesignTokens.elevation2,
177	      ),
178	      child: Column(
179	        mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,
180	        crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.stretch,
181	        children: [
182	          Row(
183	            children: [
184	              Icon(
185	                icon,
186	                size: DesignTokens.dialogIconSize,
187	                color: DesignTokens.colorPrimary,
188	              ),
189	              const SizedBox(width: DesignTokens.spacingSm),
190	              Expanded(
191	                child: Text(
192	                  title,
193	                  style: DesignTokens.textTitleSm.copyWith(color: titleColor),
194	                ),
195	              ),
196	            ],
197	          ),
198	          const SizedBox(height: DesignTokens.dialogContentGap),
199	          Text(
200	            message,
201	            style: DesignTokens.textBodyMd.copyWith(
202	              color: DesignTokens.colorTextSecondary,
203	            ),
204	          ),
205	          const SizedBox(height: DesignTokens.dialogContentGap),
206	          AppButton(label: confirmLabel, onPressed: onConfirm),
207	          if (caption != null) ...[
208	            const SizedBox(height: DesignTokens.dialogContentGap),
209	            Text(

1	import 'package:fpdart/fpdart.dart';
2	
3	import '../../../../core/failure/failure.dart';
4	
5	/// Story 2.4's one DI-singleton access point for the account's
6	/// `biometricEnabled` preference — mirrors `features/vault/domain/
7	/// repositories/vault_repository.dart`'s stream-plus-sync-getter shape
8	/// (AD-14), except the underlying source of truth is server-side (`PATCH
9	/// /account/settings`), not on-device.
10	///
11	/// [currentBiometricEnabled] is the single source both
12	/// `core/navigation/app_router.dart` (feeding `VaultLockScreen`'s
13	/// `attemptBiometricFirst`) and the Configurações toggle read — never a
14	/// second, independently-tracked copy of the same boolean.
15	abstract class AccountSettingsRepository {
16	  /// The exact [Failure.message] [setBiometricEnabled] returns when a call
17	  /// is discarded for being superseded by a newer one (the generation
18	  /// guard, `AccountSettingsRepositoryImpl._generation`) — an internal
19	  /// control-flow signal, not a real error, since the winning call already
20	  /// settled the value correctly by the time this one resolves.
21	  /// `AccountSettingsCubit` recognizes this exact string to suppress it
22	  /// from the UI rather than showing a raw, English, internal message.
23	  static const supersededMessage = 'Superseded by a newer preference update';
24	
25	  /// Broadcast stream of the current `biometricEnabled` preference. Like
26	  /// `VaultRepository.statusStream`, this always has a value from the
27	  /// moment the repository is constructed (`true`) — a late subscriber
28	  /// still immediately replays that cached value.
29	  Stream<bool> get biometricEnabledStream;
30	
31	  /// The last value emitted on [biometricEnabledStream], read
32	  /// synchronously — starts `true` (never `null`) so a cold boot before
33	  /// [fetchBiometricEnabled] resolves still degrades to "try biometric
34	  /// first" (Design Notes), never silent PIN-only.
35	  bool get currentBiometricEnabled;
36	
37	  /// Boot-time read: `PATCH /account/settings` called with `{}` — no GET
38	  /// endpoint exists for this resource (Boundaries). A successful response
39	  /// updates [currentBiometricEnabled]/[biometricEnabledStream] to the
40	  /// server's value; any [Failure] is swallowed (fire-and-forget, like
41	  /// `SessionRepository.restoreSession()`) and leaves
42	  /// [currentBiometricEnabled] exactly as it was.
43	  Future<Either<Failure, Unit>> fetchBiometricEnabled();
44	
45	  /// Story 2.4's optimistic toggle: [currentBiometricEnabled]/
46	  /// [biometricEnabledStream] flip to [enabled] immediately, before the
47	  /// `PATCH {"biometricEnabled": enabled}` call even starts (RNF01,
48	  /// <100ms) — then, on failure, revert back to the prior value and
49	  /// return `Left` so the caller can surface the `Failure`'s message. A
50	  /// successful PATCH leaves the optimistic value in place and returns
51	  /// `Right(unit)`.
52	  Future<Either<Failure, Unit>> setBiometricEnabled(bool enabled);
53	
54	  /// spec-8-3 — the profile name shown on Configurações, read by
55	  /// `AccountSettingsCubit` at construction (Boundaries: "Cubit reads
56	  /// displayName/email from the repository at construction"). Starts `''`
57	  /// (Boundaries: "default ''") and is set only from
58	  /// [fetchBiometricEnabled]'s own success branch (piggybacking on that
59	  /// call's response, Boundaries: "no new network call") or, once set,
60	  /// from a successful [setDisplayName].
61	  String get currentDisplayName;
62	
63	  /// spec-8-3 — the account's e-mail, read the same way as
64	  /// [currentDisplayName]; never written by this repository ("email is
65	  /// rejected" per the contract's own `PATCH /account/settings` summary).
66	  String get currentEmail;
67	
68	  /// spec-8-3 — writes the profile's `displayName` via
69	  /// `PATCH {"displayName": name}`. Not optimistic (Boundaries): unlike
70	  /// [setBiometricEnabled], [currentDisplayName] only changes once this
71	  /// call's PATCH actually succeeds. Guarded by its own generation counter,
72	  /// same shape as [setBiometricEnabled]'s own `_generation` guard but kept
73	  /// separate (Boundaries) — a call superseded by a newer overlapping one
74	  /// returns `Left(Failure.malformedResponse(message: supersededMessage))`
75	  /// without touching [currentDisplayName].
76	  Future<Either<Failure, Unit>> setDisplayName(String name);
77	
78	  /// Releases the underlying stream resource. Wired as `get_it`'s
79	  /// `dispose:` callback on registration, same rationale as
80	  /// `VaultRepository.dispose()`/`SessionRepository.dispose()`.
81	  Future<void> dispose();
82	}

---
title: 'Story 8.5: Account Deletion'
type: 'feature'
created: '2026-11-08'
status: 'draft'
review_loop_iteration: 0
context: []
---

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** Configurações's "Apagar conta" is a dead action — no confirmation dialog, no `DELETE /account` call (epic-8-context.md Story 8.5; FR-43, RNF05, LGPD).

**Approach:** Add a destructive-styled `ConfirmationDialog` (red title/confirm button, `Cancelar` outline) triggered by a new "Apagar conta" button; on confirm, `AccountSettingsCubit.deleteAccount()` calls the new `AccountSettingsRepository.deleteAccount()` (`DELETE /account`), then reuses `logout()`'s existing lock+logout+clear sequence (extracted into a shared private helper) — same post-action destination as Story 8.4 (FR-42), no new navigation code.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- `ConfirmationDialog` gains optional `confirmButtonColor` (null → `colorPrimary`, unchanged default) and `cancelLabel`/`onCancel` (both null together → no cancel button, exact current session-expiry shape preserved). `AppButton` gains optional `backgroundColor`, consulted only for `AppButtonVariant.primary` (mirrors `textColor`'s existing "only consulted for textGhost" convention), null → `colorPrimary`.
- "Apagar conta": `AppButtonVariant.textGhost` + `textColor: colorError`, the scroll column's last child after "Sair" (prototype-extract.md:116). Disabled while `isDeletingAccount`.
- Tap opens `ConfirmationDialog` (title `'Apagar sua conta?'`, message on permanent/irreversible LGPD deletion, `titleColor`/`confirmButtonColor: colorError`, `barrierColor: colorScrimHeavy`, `confirmLabel: 'Apagar tudo'`, `cancelLabel: 'Cancelar'`) — reuses the same focus-trap/single-overlay widget session-expiry already uses (epic-8-context.md).
- `onCancel` pops the dialog only, no network call. `onConfirm` pops the dialog synchronously, then calls `AccountSettingsCubit.deleteAccount()`.
- `AccountSettingsRepository.deleteAccount()`/`_Impl` → `AccountRemoteDataSource.deleteAccount()` → `ApiClient.delete('account-delete', data: {'confirmation': 'DELETE'})`, success mapped to `Right(unit)` (response body unused).
- `AccountSettingsCubit.deleteAccount()`: guard re-entry via new `isDeletingAccount` (mirrors `isLoggingOut`). `Left` → reset `isDeletingAccount`, set `deleteAccountErrorMessage: failure.message` (inline, `colorError`, below the button — same convention as the biometric toggle's `errorMessage`, announced via the existing `_announce` + `BlocListener` pattern). `Right` → run the same lock+session-logout+cache-clear sequence `logout()` already performs, extracted into a shared private `_finishSession()` called by both (closes spec-8-4-logout.md's own Design Notes directive).
- No navigation code: the existing `app_router.dart` redirect (already watching `VaultStatus`/`SessionStatus`) lands on `/vault` once `_finishSession()` relocks — identical to Story 8.4.

**Ask First:** None.

**Never:** a dedicated "account deleted" screen (none exists; same destination as logout, prototype-extract.md:41,197); an undo/grace-period flow; auto-retrying a failed `DELETE /account`; changing `app_router.dart`; changing `ConfirmationDialog`'s single-overlay guard.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Tap "Apagar conta" | `isDeletingAccount: false` | destructive dialog opens (red title + "Apagar tudo", outline "Cancelar") | N/A |
| Tap "Cancelar" | dialog open | dialog closes, no network call, screen unchanged | N/A |
| Tap "Apagar tudo" | dialog open | dialog closes immediately; `account-delete` fires; on success vault relocks -> redirect to `/vault`; tokens + both Hive caches clear | N/A |
| `account-delete` fails (offline/expired/...) | any | dialog already closed; inline red error below "Apagar conta"; vault stays unlocked, nothing cleared | `Left.message` shown (unlike logout's swallowed failure) |
| Double-tap "Apagar conta" | `isDeletingAccount: true` | second tap no-ops (button disabled) | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/features/account/domain/repositories/account_settings_repository.dart:76-82` -- add `deleteAccount()` before `dispose()`
- `lib/features/account/data/repositories/account_settings_repository_impl.dart:182-215` -- implement `deleteAccount()` before `dispose()`
- `lib/features/account/data/datasources/account_remote_data_source.dart:31-53` -- add `deleteAccount()` (`_apiClient.delete('account-delete', data: {'confirmation': 'DELETE'})`)
- `lib/features/account/presentation/cubit/account_settings_cubit.dart:16-158,340-397` -- state fields `isDeletingAccount`/`deleteAccountErrorMessage`; extract `_finishSession()` from `logout()`; add `deleteAccount()`
- `lib/features/account/presentation/screens/account_settings_screen.dart:569-584` -- "Apagar conta" trigger + inline error, after "Sair"; dialog builder
- `lib/core/widgets/confirmation_dialog.dart:18-148` -- `confirmButtonColor`/`cancelLabel`/`onCancel` params + second button in `_Card`
- `lib/core/widgets/app_button.dart:18-140` -- `backgroundColor` param, primary variant only
- `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml:1820-1840` (`account-delete`, bearerAuth, `{confirmation: 'DELETE'}`) + `README.md:46`
- `docs/input/prototype/cerne-prototype.html` (`askDelete`/`confirmDelete`/`cancelDelete` spans) + `prototype-extract.md:41,114,116`
- `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-8-4-logout.md` Design Notes -- the shared-helper directive this story closes
- Tests: `test/core/widgets/{app_button,confirmation_dialog}_test.dart`, `test/features/account/{data/datasources/account_remote_data_source,data/repositories/account_settings_repository_impl,presentation/cubit/account_settings_cubit,presentation/screens/account_settings_screen}_test.dart`

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [ ] `app_button.dart` -- add `backgroundColor` (primary-only)
- [ ] `confirmation_dialog.dart` -- add `confirmButtonColor`/`cancelLabel`/`onCancel`
- [ ] `account_remote_data_source.dart` -- `deleteAccount()`
- [ ] `account_settings_repository.dart`/`_impl.dart` -- `deleteAccount()`
- [ ] `account_settings_cubit.dart` -- `isDeletingAccount`/`deleteAccountErrorMessage`, `_finishSession()` extraction, `deleteAccount()`
- [ ] `account_settings_screen.dart` -- "Apagar conta" button, dialog wiring, inline error
- [ ] Tests: I/O matrix + new unit coverage; extend `AppButton`/`ConfirmationDialog` fixtures for the new params

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given Configurações, when "Apagar conta" is tapped, then the destructive-variant dialog appears with a red title (epics.md Story 8.5 AC).
- Given the dialog, when "Apagar tudo" is confirmed, then `DELETE /account` fires and, on success, the account/data are gone and the user lands on the same destination as logout.
- Given "Cancelar" is tapped, then no network call fires and the screen is unchanged.

## Design Notes

`AppButton`'s primary-variant pressed-state overlay stays `colorPrimaryPressed` even when `backgroundColor` overrides the fill to `colorError` — the prototype's static mockup defines no distinct pressed-red value, and design_tokens.dart has none either; inventing one would violate "never hardcode a visual value outside design_tokens.dart." Accepted as a cosmetic, sub-200ms imperfection, not a blocking gap.

`deleteAccount()`'s success path still calls `_sessionRepository.logout()` (POST `auth-logout`) after the account is already server-side deleted — harmless and intentional: it's the same shared `_finishSession()` Story 8.4 built, and epic-8-context.md explicitly directs reusing it rather than branching.

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `fvm flutter analyze` -- expected: zero issues
- `fvm flutter test test/core/widgets test/features/account test/core/navigation` -- expected: all pass

---
title: 'Story 8.5: Account Deletion'
type: 'feature'
created: '2026-11-08'
status: 'ready-for-dev'
review_loop_iteration: 0
context: []
---

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** Configurações's "Apagar conta" is a dead action — no confirmation dialog, no `DELETE /account` call (epic-8-context.md Story 8.5; FR-43, RNF05, LGPD).

**Approach:** Add a destructive-styled `ConfirmationDialog` (red title/confirm button, `Cancelar` outline) triggered by a new "Apagar conta" button; on confirm, `AccountSettingsCubit.deleteAccount()` calls the new `AccountSettingsRepository.deleteAccount()` (`DELETE /account`), then reuses `logout()`'s existing lock+logout+clear sequence (extracted into a shared private helper) — same post-action destination as Story 8.4 (FR-42), no new navigation code.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- `ConfirmationDialog` gains optional `confirmButtonColor` (null → `colorPrimary`, unchanged default) and `cancelLabel`/`onCancel` (both null together → no cancel button, exact current session-expiry shape preserved). `AppButton` gains optional `backgroundColor`, consulted only for `AppButtonVariant.primary` (mirrors `textColor`'s existing "only consulted for textGhost" convention), null → `colorPrimary`.
- "Apagar conta": `AppButtonVariant.textGhost` + `textColor: colorError`, the scroll column's last child after "Sair" (prototype-extract.md:116). Disabled while `isDeletingAccount`.
- Tap opens `ConfirmationDialog` (title `'Apagar sua conta?'`, message on permanent/irreversible LGPD deletion, `titleColor`/`confirmButtonColor: colorError`, `barrierColor: colorScrimHeavy`, `confirmLabel: 'Apagar tudo'`, `cancelLabel: 'Cancelar'`) — reuses the same focus-trap/single-overlay widget session-expiry already uses (epic-8-context.md).
- `onCancel` pops the dialog only, no network call. `onConfirm` pops the dialog synchronously, then calls `AccountSettingsCubit.deleteAccount()`.
- `AccountSettingsRepository.deleteAccount()`/`_Impl` → `AccountRemoteDataSource.deleteAccount()` → `ApiClient.delete('account-delete', data: {'confirmation': 'DELETE'})`, success mapped to `Right(unit)` (response body unused).
- `AccountSettingsCubit.deleteAccount()`: guard re-entry via new `isDeletingAccount` (mirrors `isLoggingOut`). `Left` → reset `isDeletingAccount`, set `deleteAccountErrorMessage: failure.message` (inline, `colorError`, below the button — same convention as the biometric toggle's `errorMessage`, announced via the existing `_announce` + `BlocListener` pattern). `Right` → run the same lock+session-logout+cache-clear sequence `logout()` already performs, extracted into a shared private `_finishSession()` called by both (closes spec-8-4-logout.md's own Design Notes directive).
- No navigation code: the existing `app_router.dart` redirect (already watching `VaultStatus`/`SessionStatus`) lands on `/vault` once `_finishSession()` relocks — identical to Story 8.4.

**Ask First:** None.

**Never:** a dedicated "account deleted" screen (none exists; same destination as logout, prototype-extract.md:41,197); an undo/grace-period flow; auto-retrying a failed `DELETE /account`; changing `app_router.dart`; changing `ConfirmationDialog`'s single-overlay guard.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Tap "Apagar conta" | `isDeletingAccount: false` | destructive dialog opens (red title + "Apagar tudo", outline "Cancelar") | N/A |
| Tap "Cancelar" | dialog open | dialog closes, no network call, screen unchanged | N/A |
| Tap "Apagar tudo" | dialog open | dialog closes immediately; `account-delete` fires; on success vault relocks -> redirect to `/vault`; tokens + both Hive caches clear | N/A |
| `account-delete` fails (offline/expired/...) | any | dialog already closed; inline red error below "Apagar conta"; vault stays unlocked, nothing cleared | `Left.message` shown (unlike logout's swallowed failure) |
| Double-tap "Apagar conta" | `isDeletingAccount: true` | second tap no-ops (button disabled) | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/features/account/domain/repositories/account_settings_repository.dart:76-82` -- add `deleteAccount()` before `dispose()`
- `lib/features/account/data/repositories/account_settings_repository_impl.dart:182-215` -- implement `deleteAccount()` before `dispose()`
- `lib/features/account/data/datasources/account_remote_data_source.dart:31-53` -- add `deleteAccount()` (`_apiClient.delete('account-delete', data: {'confirmation': 'DELETE'})`)
- `lib/features/account/presentation/cubit/account_settings_cubit.dart:16-158,340-397` -- state fields `isDeletingAccount`/`deleteAccountErrorMessage`; extract `_finishSession()` from `logout()`; add `deleteAccount()`
- `lib/features/account/presentation/screens/account_settings_screen.dart:569-584` -- "Apagar conta" trigger + inline error, after "Sair"; dialog builder
- `lib/core/widgets/confirmation_dialog.dart:18-148` -- `confirmButtonColor`/`cancelLabel`/`onCancel` params + second button in `_Card`
- `lib/core/widgets/app_button.dart:18-140` -- `backgroundColor` param, primary variant only
- `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml:1820-1840` (`account-delete`, bearerAuth, `{confirmation: 'DELETE'}`) + `README.md:46`
- `docs/input/prototype/cerne-prototype.html` (`askDelete`/`confirmDelete`/`cancelDelete` spans) + `prototype-extract.md:41,114,116`
- `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-8-4-logout.md` Design Notes -- the shared-helper directive this story closes
- Tests: `test/core/widgets/{app_button,confirmation_dialog}_test.dart`, `test/features/account/{data/datasources/account_remote_data_source,data/repositories/account_settings_repository_impl,presentation/cubit/account_settings_cubit,presentation/screens/account_settings_screen}_test.dart`

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [ ] `app_button.dart` -- add `backgroundColor` (primary-only)
- [ ] `confirmation_dialog.dart` -- add `confirmButtonColor`/`cancelLabel`/`onCancel`
- [ ] `account_remote_data_source.dart` -- `deleteAccount()`
- [ ] `account_settings_repository.dart`/`_impl.dart` -- `deleteAccount()`
- [ ] `account_settings_cubit.dart` -- `isDeletingAccount`/`deleteAccountErrorMessage`, `_finishSession()` extraction, `deleteAccount()`
- [ ] `account_settings_screen.dart` -- "Apagar conta" button, dialog wiring, inline error
- [ ] Tests: I/O matrix + new unit coverage; extend `AppButton`/`ConfirmationDialog` fixtures for the new params

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given Configurações, when "Apagar conta" is tapped, then the destructive-variant dialog appears with a red title (epics.md Story 8.5 AC).
- Given the dialog, when "Apagar tudo" is confirmed, then `DELETE /account` fires and, on success, the account/data are gone and the user lands on the same destination as logout.
- Given "Cancelar" is tapped, then no network call fires and the screen is unchanged.

## Design Notes

`AppButton`'s primary-variant pressed-state overlay stays `colorPrimaryPressed` even when `backgroundColor` overrides the fill to `colorError` — the prototype's static mockup defines no distinct pressed-red value, and design_tokens.dart has none either; inventing one would violate "never hardcode a visual value outside design_tokens.dart." Accepted as a cosmetic, sub-200ms imperfection, not a blocking gap.

`deleteAccount()`'s success path still calls `_sessionRepository.logout()` (POST `auth-logout`) after the account is already server-side deleted — harmless and intentional: it's the same shared `_finishSession()` Story 8.4 built, and epic-8-context.md explicitly directs reusing it rather than branching.

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `fvm flutter analyze` -- expected: zero issues
- `fvm flutter test test/core/widgets test/features/account test/core/navigation` -- expected: all pass

# Sync Sprint Status

Shared sub-step for updating `sprint-status.yaml` during build. Called from any route (plan-code-review, one-shot, future routes) with a `target_status` parameter.

## Preconditions

Skip this entire file (return to caller) if ANY of:
- `story_key` is unset
- `/Users/wagnerduarte/Documents/Faculdade/2026.2/TCC/cerne-ciclo-b/_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/sprint-status.yaml` does not exist on disk

## Instructions

1. Load the FULL `/Users/wagnerduarte/Documents/Faculdade/2026.2/TCC/cerne-ciclo-b/_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/sprint-status.yaml` file.
2. Find the `development_status` entry matching `{story_key}`. If not found, warn the user once (`"{story_key} not found in sprint-status; skipping sprint sync"`) and return to caller.
3. **Idempotency check.** If `development_status[{story_key}]` is already at `target_status` or a later state (`review` is later than `in-progress`; `done` is later than both), return to caller — no write needed. Never regress a story's status.
4. Set `development_status[{story_key}]` to `{target_status}`.
5. **Epic lift (only when `target_status` = `in-progress`).** Derive the parent epic key as `epic-{N}` from the leading numeric segment of `{story_key}` (e.g., `3-2-digest-delivery` → `epic-3`). If that entry exists and is `backlog`, set it to `in-progress`. Leave it alone otherwise. Skip this sub-step entirely when `target_status` is not `in-progress`.
6. Refresh `last_updated` to the current date.
7. Save the file, preserving ALL comments and structure including STATUS DEFINITIONS and WORKFLOW NOTES.

1	---
2	title: 'Story 8.5: Account Deletion'
3	type: 'feature'
4	created: '2026-11-08'
5	status: 'done'
6	review_loop_iteration: 0
7	context: []
8	baseline_commit: '45b2dcd7ef5d7e7a5d8434ed4b1cfabbc3df43c4'
9	---
10	
11	<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">
12	
13	## Intent
14	
15	**Problem:** Configurações's "Apagar conta" is a dead action — no confirmation dialog, no `DELETE /account` call (epic-8-context.md Story 8.5; FR-43, RNF05, LGPD).
16	
17	**Approach:** Add a destructive-styled `ConfirmationDialog` (red title/confirm button, `Cancelar` outline) triggered by a new "Apagar conta" button; on confirm, `AccountSettingsCubit.deleteAccount()` calls the new `AccountSettingsRepository.deleteAccount()` (`DELETE /account`), then reuses `logout()`'s existing lock+logout+clear sequence (extracted into a shared private helper) — same post-action destination as Story 8.4 (FR-42), no new navigation code.
18	
19	## Boundaries & Constraints
20	
21	**Always:**
22	- `ConfirmationDialog` gains optional `confirmButtonColor` (null → `colorPrimary`, unchanged default) and `cancelLabel`/`onCancel` (both null together → no cancel button, exact current session-expiry shape preserved). `AppButton` gains optional `backgroundColor`, consulted only for `AppButtonVariant.primary` (mirrors `textColor`'s existing "only consulted for textGhost" convention), null → `colorPrimary`.
23	- "Apagar conta": `AppButtonVariant.textGhost` + `textColor: colorError`, the scroll column's last child after "Sair" (prototype-extract.md:116). Disabled while `isDeletingAccount`.
24	- Tap opens `ConfirmationDialog` (title `'Apagar sua conta?'`, message on permanent/irreversible LGPD deletion, `titleColor`/`confirmButtonColor: colorError`, `barrierColor: colorScrimHeavy`, `confirmLabel: 'Apagar tudo'`, `cancelLabel: 'Cancelar'`) — reuses the same focus-trap/single-overlay widget session-expiry already uses (epic-8-context.md).
25	- `onCancel` pops the dialog only, no network call. `onConfirm` pops the dialog synchronously, then calls `AccountSettingsCubit.deleteAccount()`.
26	- `AccountSettingsRepository.deleteAccount()`/`_Impl` → `AccountRemoteDataSource.deleteAccount()` → `ApiClient.delete('account-delete', data: {'confirmation': 'DELETE'})`, success mapped to `Right(unit)` (response body unused).
27	- `AccountSettingsCubit.deleteAccount()`: guard re-entry via new `isDeletingAccount` (mirrors `isLoggingOut`). `Left` → reset `isDeletingAccount`, set `deleteAccountErrorMessage: failure.message` (inline, `colorError`, below the button — same convention as the biometric toggle's `errorMessage`, announced via the existing `_announce` + `BlocListener` pattern). `Right` → run the same lock+session-logout+cache-clear sequence `logout()` already performs, extracted into a shared private `_finishSession()` called by both (closes spec-8-4-logout.md's own Design Notes directive).
28	- No navigation code: the existing `app_router.dart` redirect (already watching `VaultStatus`/`SessionStatus`) lands on `/vault` once `_finishSession()` relocks — identical to Story 8.4.
29	
30	**Ask First:** None.
31	
32	**Never:** a dedicated "account deleted" screen (none exists; same destination as logout, prototype-extract.md:41,197); an undo/grace-period flow; auto-retrying a failed `DELETE /account`; changing `app_router.dart`; changing `ConfirmationDialog`'s single-overlay guard.
33	
34	## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix
35	
36	| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
37	|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
38	| Tap "Apagar conta" | `isDeletingAccount: false` | destructive dialog opens (red title + "Apagar tudo", outline "Cancelar") | N/A |
39	| Tap "Cancelar" | dialog open | dialog closes, no network call, screen unchanged | N/A |
40	| Tap "Apagar tudo" | dialog open | dialog closes immediately; `account-delete` fires; on success vault relocks -> redirect to `/vault`; tokens + both Hive caches clear | N/A |
41	| `account-delete` fails (offline/expired/...) | any | dialog already closed; inline red error below "Apagar conta"; vault stays unlocked, nothing cleared | `Left.message` shown (unlike logout's swallowed failure) |
42	| Double-tap "Apagar conta" | `isDeletingAccount: true` | second tap no-ops (button disabled) | N/A |
43	
44	</frozen-after-approval>
45	
46	## Code Map
47	
48	- `lib/features/account/domain/repositories/account_settings_repository.dart:76-82` -- add `deleteAccount()` before `dispose()`
49	- `lib/features/account/data/repositories/account_settings_repository_impl.dart:182-215` -- implement `deleteAccount()` before `dispose()`
50	- `lib/features/account/data/datasources/account_remote_data_source.dart:31-53` -- add `deleteAccount()` (`_apiClient.delete('account-delete', data: {'confirmation': 'DELETE'})`)
51	- `lib/features/account/presentation/cubit/account_settings_cubit.dart:16-158,340-397` -- state fields `isDeletingAccount`/`deleteAccountErrorMessage`; extract `_finishSession()` from `logout()`; add `deleteAccount()`
52	- `lib/features/account/presentation/screens/account_settings_screen.dart:569-584` -- "Apagar conta" trigger + inline error, after "Sair"; dialog builder
53	- `lib/core/widgets/confirmation_dialog.dart:18-148` -- `confirmButtonColor`/`cancelLabel`/`onCancel` params + second button in `_Card`
54	- `lib/core/widgets/app_button.dart:18-140` -- `backgroundColor` param, primary variant only
55	- `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml:1820-1840` (`account-delete`, bearerAuth, `{confirmation: 'DELETE'}`) + `README.md:46`
56	- `docs/input/prototype/cerne-prototype.html` (`askDelete`/`confirmDelete`/`cancelDelete` spans) + `prototype-extract.md:41,114,116`
57	- `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-8-4-logout.md` Design Notes -- the shared-helper directive this story closes
58	- Tests: `test/core/widgets/{app_button,confirmation_dialog}_test.dart`, `test/features/account/{data/datasources/account_remote_data_source,data/repositories/account_settings_repository_impl,presentation/cubit/account_settings_cubit,presentation/screens/account_settings_screen}_test.dart`
59	
60	## Tasks & Acceptance
61	
62	**Execution:**
63	- [x] `app_button.dart` -- add `backgroundColor` (primary-only)
64	- [x] `confirmation_dialog.dart` -- add `confirmButtonColor`/`cancelLabel`/`onCancel`
65	- [x] `account_remote_data_source.dart` -- `deleteAccount()`
66	- [x] `account_settings_repository.dart`/`_impl.dart` -- `deleteAccount()`

68	- [x] `account_settings_screen.dart` -- "Apagar conta" button, dialog wiring, inline error
69	- [x] Tests: I/O matrix + new unit coverage; extend `AppButton`/`ConfirmationDialog` fixtures for the new params
70	
71	**Acceptance Criteria:**
72	- Given Configurações, when "Apagar conta" is tapped, then the destructive-variant dialog appears with a red title (epics.md Story 8.5 AC).
73	- Given the dialog, when "Apagar tudo" is confirmed, then `DELETE /account` fires and, on success, the account/data are gone and the user lands on the same destination as logout.
74	- Given "Cancelar" is tapped, then no network call fires and the screen is unchanged.
75	
76	## Design Notes
77	
78	`AppButton`'s primary-variant pressed-state overlay stays `colorPrimaryPressed` even when `backgroundColor` overrides the fill to `colorError` — the prototype's static mockup defines no distinct pressed-red value, and design_tokens.dart has none either; inventing one would violate "never hardcode a visual value outside design_tokens.dart." Accepted as a cosmetic, sub-200ms imperfection, not a blocking gap.

## Intent

**Problem:** Configurações's "Apagar conta" is a dead action — no confirmation dialog, no `DELETE /account` call (epic-8-context.md Story 8.5; FR-43, RNF05, LGPD).

**Approach:** Add a destructive-styled `ConfirmationDialog` (red title/confirm button, `Cancelar` outline) triggered by a new "Apagar conta" button; on confirm, `AccountSettingsCubit.deleteAccount()` calls the new `AccountSettingsRepository.deleteAccount()` (`DELETE /account`), then reuses `logout()`'s existing lock+logout+clear sequence (extracted into a shared private helper) — same post-action destination as Story 8.4 (FR-42), no new navigation code.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- `ConfirmationDialog` gains optional `confirmButtonColor` (null → `colorPrimary`, unchanged default) and `cancelLabel`/`onCancel` (both null together → no cancel button, exact current session-expiry shape preserved). `AppButton` gains optional `backgroundColor`, consulted only for `AppButtonVariant.primary` (mirrors `textColor`'s existing "only consulted for textGhost" convention), null → `colorPrimary`.
- "Apagar conta": `AppButtonVariant.textGhost` + `textColor: colorError`, the scroll column's last child after "Sair" (prototype-extract.md:116). Disabled while `isDeletingAccount`.
- Tap opens `ConfirmationDialog` (title `'Apagar sua conta?'`, message on permanent/irreversible LGPD deletion, `titleColor`/`confirmButtonColor: colorError`, `barrierColor: colorScrimHeavy`, `confirmLabel: 'Apagar tudo'`, `cancelLabel: 'Cancelar'`) — reuses the same focus-trap/single-overlay widget session-expiry already uses (epic-8-context.md).
- `onCancel` pops the dialog only, no network call. `onConfirm` pops the dialog synchronously, then calls `AccountSettingsCubit.deleteAccount()`.
- `AccountSettingsRepository.deleteAccount()`/`_Impl` → `AccountRemoteDataSource.deleteAccount()` → `ApiClient.delete('account-delete', data: {'confirmation': 'DELETE'})`, success mapped to `Right(unit)` (response body unused).
- `AccountSettingsCubit.deleteAccount()`: guard re-entry via new `isDeletingAccount` (mirrors `isLoggingOut`). `Left` → reset `isDeletingAccount`, set `deleteAccountErrorMessage: failure.message` (inline, `colorError`, below the button — same convention as the biometric toggle's `errorMessage`, announced via the existing `_announce` + `BlocListener` pattern). `Right` → run the same lock+session-logout+cache-clear sequence `logout()` already performs, extracted into a shared private `_finishSession()` called by both (closes spec-8-4-logout.md's own Design Notes directive).
- No navigation code: the existing `app_router.dart` redirect (already watching `VaultStatus`/`SessionStatus`) lands on `/vault` once `_finishSession()` relocks — identical to Story 8.4.

**Ask First:** None.

**Never:** a dedicated "account deleted" screen (none exists; same destination as logout, prototype-extract.md:41,197); an undo/grace-period flow; auto-retrying a failed `DELETE /account`; changing `app_router.dart`; changing `ConfirmationDialog`'s single-overlay guard.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Tap "Apagar conta" | `isDeletingAccount: false` | destructive dialog opens (red title + "Apagar tudo", outline "Cancelar") | N/A |
| Tap "Cancelar" | dialog open | dialog closes, no network call, screen unchanged | N/A |
| Tap "Apagar tudo" | dialog open | dialog closes immediately; `account-delete` fires; on success vault relocks -> redirect to `/vault`; tokens + both Hive caches clear | N/A |
| `account-delete` fails (offline/expired/...) | any | dialog already closed; inline red error below "Apagar conta"; vault stays unlocked, nothing cleared | `Left.message` shown (unlike logout's swallowed failure) |
| Double-tap "Apagar conta" | `isDeletingAccount: true` | second tap no-ops (button disabled) | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/features/account/domain/repositories/account_settings_repository.dart:76-82` -- add `deleteAccount()` before `dispose()`
- `lib/features/account/data/repositories/account_settings_repository_impl.dart:182-215` -- implement `deleteAccount()` before `dispose()`
- `lib/features/account/data/datasources/account_remote_data_source.dart:31-53` -- add `deleteAccount()` (`_apiClient.delete('account-delete', data: {'confirmation': 'DELETE'})`)
- `lib/features/account/presentation/cubit/account_settings_cubit.dart:16-158,340-397` -- state fields `isDeletingAccount`/`deleteAccountErrorMessage`; extract `_finishSession()` from `logout()`; add `deleteAccount()`
- `lib/features/account/presentation/screens/account_settings_screen.dart:569-584` -- "Apagar conta" trigger + inline error, after "Sair"; dialog builder
- `lib/core/widgets/confirmation_dialog.dart:18-148` -- `confirmButtonColor`/`cancelLabel`/`onCancel` params + second button in `_Card`
- `lib/core/widgets/app_button.dart:18-140` -- `backgroundColor` param, primary variant only
- `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml:1820-1840` (`account-delete`, bearerAuth, `{confirmation: 'DELETE'}`) + `README.md:46`
- `docs/input/prototype/cerne-prototype.html` (`askDelete`/`confirmDelete`/`cancelDelete` spans) + `prototype-extract.md:41,114,116`
- `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-8-4-logout.md` Design Notes -- the shared-helper directive this story closes
- Tests: `test/core/widgets/{app_button,confirmation_dialog}_test.dart`, `test/features/account/{data/datasources/account_remote_data_source,data/repositories/account_settings_repository_impl,presentation/cubit/account_settings_cubit,presentation/screens/account_settings_screen}_test.dart`

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [x] `app_button.dart` -- add `backgroundColor` (primary-only)
- [x] `confirmation_dialog.dart` -- add `confirmButtonColor`/`cancelLabel`/`onCancel`
- [x] `account_remote_data_source.dart` -- `deleteAccount()`
- [x] `account_settings_repository.dart`/`_impl.dart` -- `deleteAccount()`
- [x] `account_settings_cubit.dart` -- `isDeletingAccount`/`deleteAccountErrorMessage`, `_finishSession()` extraction, `deleteAccount()`
- [x] `account_settings_screen.dart` -- "Apagar conta" button, dialog wiring, inline error
- [x] Tests: I/O matrix + new unit coverage; extend `AppButton`/`ConfirmationDialog` fixtures for the new params

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given Configurações, when "Apagar conta" is tapped, then the destructive-variant dialog appears with a red title (epics.md Story 8.5 AC).
- Given the dialog, when "Apagar tudo" is confirmed, then `DELETE /account` fires and, on success, the account/data are gone and the user lands on the same destination as logout.
- Given "Cancelar" is tapped, then no network call fires and the screen is unchanged.

## Design Notes

`AppButton`'s primary-variant pressed-state overlay stays `colorPrimaryPressed` even when `backgroundColor` overrides the fill to `colorError` — the prototype's static mockup defines no distinct pressed-red value, and design_tokens.dart has none either; inventing one would violate "never hardcode a visual value outside design_tokens.dart." Accepted as a cosmetic, sub-200ms imperfection, not a blocking gap.

`deleteAccount()`'s success path still calls `_sessionRepository.logout()` (POST `auth-logout`) after the account is already server-side deleted — harmless and intentional: it's the same shared `_finishSession()` Story 8.4 built, and epic-8-context.md explicitly directs reusing it rather than branching.

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `fvm flutter analyze` -- expected: zero issues
- `fvm flutter test test/core/widgets test/features/account test/core/navigation` -- expected: all pass

# Step 4: Review

## RULES

- **Language** — Speak in `English`. Write any file output in `English`.
- All review subagents must run at the same model capability as the current session.
- Run subagents synchronously: launch them together, then wait for all results before continuing.

## INSTRUCTIONS

Change `{spec_file}` status to `in-review` in the frontmatter before continuing.

### Construct Diff

Read `{baseline_commit}` from `{spec_file}` frontmatter. If `{baseline_commit}` is missing or `NO_VCS`, use best effort to determine what changed. Otherwise, construct `{diff_output}` covering all changes — tracked and untracked — since `{baseline_commit}`.

Do NOT `git add` anything — this is read-only inspection.

### Review

Execute these review layers in parallel wherever their execution methods allow: substitute the runtime placeholders (e.g. `{diff_output}`) into each layer's instruction. When an instruction launches a reviewer subagent, launch that child with the prompt text after placeholder substitution; do not load the reviewer instruction file yourself. For any other customized instruction, execute it as written. Parallel means several blocking calls awaited together in this turn — never backgrounded or detached, never ending the turn to await results. When running layers as subagents, spawn every reviewer before reading or reacting to any of their output; begin collection and triage only once all are launched.

#### Blind Hunter (`blind-hunter`)

Launch a context-free subagent with this prompt:

Conduct a review of CONTENT.
Look for what's missing, not only what's wrong.
Find at least ten issues to fix or improve.
Output a Markdown list of findings only — no severity, priority, or ranking.
If the content is empty, stop and say so.
If you have zero findings, re-check and keep thinking; do not stop with an empty list.

CONTENT:
{diff_output}

Do not invoke any skill. Return only the review result.

#### Edge Case Hunter (`edge-case-hunter`)

Launch a context-free subagent with this prompt:

Read `/Users/wagnerduarte/Documents/Faculdade/2026.2/TCC/cerne-ciclo-b/_bmad/render/bmad-build/cerne-ciclo-b-f3acac58e4e4/23bb7dc2d569f6e2d208/review-prompts/edge-case-hunter.md` completely and follow it as your review instructions.

Review content:

{diff_output}

Do not invoke any skill. If the instruction file is unreadable, report that exact failure and stop. Return only the review result.

#### Verification Gap Reviewer (`verification-gap`)

Launch a context-free subagent with this prompt:

Read `/Users/wagnerduarte/Documents/Faculdade/2026.2/TCC/cerne-ciclo-b/_bmad/render/bmad-build/cerne-ciclo-b-f3acac58e4e4/23bb7dc2d569f6e2d208/review-prompts/verification-gap.md` completely and follow it as your review instructions.

Review content:

{diff_output}

Do not invoke any skill. If the instruction file is unreadable, report that exact failure and stop. Return only the review result.

If a layer's instruction requires subagents and none are available, for each such layer write under `/Users/wagnerduarte/Documents/Faculdade/2026.2/TCC/cerne-ciclo-b/_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts` the exact child prompt from that layer's instruction after placeholder substitution (not a path-only pointer), then HALT. Ask the human to run each in a separate session (ideally a different LLM) and paste back the findings.

### Classify

1. Deduplicate only findings with the same claim and same required action. Then evaluate each remaining finding independently. Do not reject a finding because a related finding was rejected.
2. Assign severity to each finding by consequence for the artifact's main consumer (software user, document reader, etc).
   Disregard any severity assigned by a reviewing subagent. Review subagents operate under by-design information asymmetry and do not have enough context to set final severity for this workflow.
   - `low`: none or cosmetic
   - `medium`: tolerable
   - `high`: intolerable
3. Route each finding into exactly one triage category. The first three categories are **this story's problem** — caused or exposed by the current change. The last two are **not this story's problem**.
   - **intent_gap** — caused by the change; cannot be resolved from the spec because the captured intent is incomplete. Do not infer intent unless there is exactly one possible reading.
   - **bad_spec** — caused by the change, including direct deviations from spec. The spec should have been clear enough to prevent it. When in doubt between bad_spec and patch, prefer bad_spec — a spec-level fix is more likely to produce coherent code.

type: 'feature'
created: '2026-11-08'
status: 'done'
